title: Monthly Recording Review — July
objective: Measure whether the monthly-recording-review craftbook assesses every recording in the index against last month's marks and lands on exactly one next-month focus.
prompt: end of the month — can you go thru the recordings index and my notes and write the review? report.md please

setup.about: Music practice project. Monthly practice recordings are indexed in workspace/recordings/index.json with a listening-notes file per recording; past monthly reviews live under workspace/reviews.
setup.missionObjectives: Once a month, review the recordings against last month's marks — proof over impression — and pick one focus for next month. Grounded in the seeded index and notes; no live services, no real credentials.

files.content:
# Listening notes — 2026-07-05 nocturne

Tempo 88 bpm. Left hand steadier than June — the arpeggios no longer bulge on beat three. Bar 12 ornaments still uneven, rushed on the second turn. Pedal is cleaner in the opening eight bars. Bar 32 run attempted at tempo: fell apart, restarted.

# Listening notes — 2026-07-12 nocturne

Tempo 92 bpm. Bar 32 run holds at 85 in isolation but breaks in context. Dynamics are starting to appear — the first real crescendo shaping in bars 17-24. Ending chord voicing much better than the June recordings.

# Listening notes — 2026-07-19 bach invention

First hands-together recording. 66 bpm, down from the 72 achieved hands-separate — expected. Evenness between the hands is good for a first attempt. Ornaments omitted for now. No memory slips.

# Listening notes — 2026-07-26 nocturne full run-through

First complete run-through ever recorded. 90 bpm working tempo. One stumble at bar 32 (recovered without stopping — new). Rubato in the middle section sounds intentional for the first time. The June recordings had no complete take at all.

# Monthly review — June 2026

## Marks

- Chopin Nocturne Op. 9 No. 2 — 84 bpm working tempo, no complete take; left hand bulges on beat three; bar 32 run avoided entirely.
- Bach Invention No. 8 — hands separate only, 72 bpm.

## Focus for July

One focus: left-hand evenness in the nocturne. Everything else is secondary.

success.summary: report.md assesses every indexed recording with concrete evidence, states deltas against the June review, gives a verdict on June's focus, and names exactly one focus for August.
